title: Establish the canonical device and build inventory
description:
Create the single canonical inventory of existing devices, board revisions, firmware/build artifacts and available evidence from records. Distinguish the documented T-Echo, T1000-E and Heltec units from proposed RAK, SDR or concentrator equipment. Verify actual manifest, resolved source, SDK and driver revisions.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Read-only records and source inspection; no device ports or physical probing. authority.01 derives authorization tuples from this artifact rather than duplicating inventory. Missing equipment is not permission to contact owners, arrange access or purchase it.
acceptance_criteria: Every entry has provenance, an exact known identifier/build or an explicit unknown. Report manifest/toolchain/API mismatches instead of assuming one fixed Zephyr version or skipping work. Existing historical validation is tied to its original configuration and is not relabeled current CCP2 qualification.
